explanation: The vulnerable code compares attacker-supplied API keys against stored per-user API keys with Python's '==' operator inside a loop, which short-circuits on the first mismatched character and leaks a timing side channel (CWE-208) exploitable to recover API keys character-by-character. The fixed code replaces this with hmac.compare_digest, a constant-time comparison, directly eliminating the observable timing difference. This is genuine security-sensitive cryptographic comparison misuse in first-party authentication code (FilebasedUserManager.find_user), matching CRYPTO-013/CWE-208, and the patch materializes the fix.
finding: API key validated via short-circuiting equality ('==') comparison in FilebasedUserManager.find_user, creating a timing side channel (CWE-208); use hmac.compare_digest for constant-time comparison.
note: Code pair is complete and self-consistent with the advisory and fix commit. Advisory itself notes the attack is theoretical with no achieved PoC and depends on network latency/noise, supporting a reduced severity. No license information supplied; 'hmac' import is assumed present in the fixed file but not shown.
